questions: Who is awake earliest, and who needs quiet then?
What do you enjoy in a hotel, and what would be inconvenient at home?
Which three outcomes should survive a budget reduction?
approval: Routines and priorities are specific
Taste references analysed into observable attributes
Budget scope and exclusions understood
Reference images tagged into attributes and style weights; used to oversample, not as rules
method: Translate each routine into a requirement with an identifier, priority and observable test.
Read references for proportion, palette, texture, lighting and atmosphere; obtain client response to a small illustrated direction.
Record disagreement, maintenance tolerance and budget trade-offs before asking for approval.

Tag every client reference image into observable attributes (materials, palette, light types, furniture forms, room type) and weight styles. Flag physically questionable features in generated images. Keep coverage of other styles.
stages.worked_example: Two adults work at home; children sleep before weekly guests leave. Brief separates study calls and sleeping access from entertaining. Warm timber is a pilot preference, not a universal luxury requirement.
failures: Failure: asking the client to choose duct sizes. Remedy: ask about noise, sleep and room use; develop technical implications in Systems.
Failure: calling every large room luxurious. Remedy: test routines and prioritise useful space in Fit.

stages.name: Ground
questions: Where would you want to sit outside at breakfast?
Which neighbouring views or noises bother you?
approval: Surveyed facts separated from assumptions
Sun wind views and noise inform orientation
Landscape water and access conflicts recorded
Site weather file summarised: comfort, sun path, wind, cooling degree-days
method: Inventory boundaries, existing buildings, trees, levels, access and utilities; attach provenance to each fact.
Draw true north, views, noise, seasonal shade and neighbours on one diagram. Test seasonal solar geometry using actual latitude.
Keep tree roots, drainage, equipment and garden paths in the same site strategy; do not substitute planting imagery for a maintainable landscape.
Load the site weather file (EPW) and summarise comfort hours, sun path, wind and cooling degree-days before choosing orientation.
stages.worked_example: Pilot ground is a fictional 30 by 40 metre rectangle in a northern-hemisphere hot-dry scenario; road south and views north. These are known scenario inputs, not surveyed facts. Summer wind is an assumption needing weather evidence.
failures: Failure: copying Australian north-facing heating advice. Remedy: recompute seasonal sun for the actual hemisphere; reopen Order and Systems.
Failure: trees shown over a service trench. Remedy: coordinate root space and utility routes before room placement.

stages.name: Fit
questions: Would you give up a second lounge to keep a larger garden?
Does the budget include furniture, landscape and professional fees?
approval: Net and gross areas reconciled
Cost assumptions and exclusions explicit
Outdoor and service space retained
method: Schedule individual usable room areas, then separately add circulation, walls, structural zones and service space without double counting.
Compare totals and each storey footprint with supplied physical constraints; statutory inputs, if supplied, remain externally established.
Show cost scenarios with currency, date, rate provenance, exclusions and contingency. Without rates report cost unresolved; never invent a local estimate.
stages.worked_example: Pilot usable rooms total 272 square metres. Circulation 40, walls 32, structural zones 12 and services 14 give 370 square metres against a 400 square metre scenario allowance. These allowances are project assumptions; no net-to-gross benchmark is asserted.
failures: Failure: gross area passes but ground-floor rooms exceed the footprint. Remedy: reconcile each level and reopen Order.
Failure: beautiful courtyard consumes circulation allowance. Remedy: recalculate and present a brief trade-off.
quantitative_checks: Area arithmetic with explicit project assumptions

method: Compare compact bar, courtyard and separated pavilion organisations using the same brief and area definitions.
Draw arrival, adjacency, private circulation, massing and at least one section together; test indoor-outdoor thresholds.
Overlay tentative supports, spans, stairs, wet stacks and main service paths. Flag unsized spans; never imply engineering certification.
Recommend one with reasons, diagram, evidence, cost/space/maintenance consequences and a client decision. Obtain a separately authored critique.
Draw massing, openings, shading and envelope material together; compare concepts' cooling load per square metre and solar gain under identical assumptions.
Generate many variants per parti, score them with the calibrated critic, and present three from different partis with their trade-offs.
stages.worked_example: Pilot recommends a compact garden bar: private hall bypasses living and stacked service core limits distribution. Courtyard improves sheltered outdoor life but uses more envelope; pavilion exposes bedrooms to the hosting route and needs an unresolved long span.
failures: Failure: spectacular glazing hides structural depth and glare. Remedy: draw the section with shading, beam zone and curtains; reopen Fit if necessary.
Failure: bedroom access crosses the party. Remedy: reserve a private hall, then recalculate area.

stages.name: Rooms
questions: Where do you put luggage, laundry and devices?
Can one person dress while another sleeps?
approval: Daily activities and furniture access tested
Doors curtains and storage coordinate
Interior and exterior dimensions reconcile
method: Use measured geometry for room boundaries and actual furniture sizes; show doors, drawers, chair use, luggage and bed-making routes.
Resolve kitchens, bathrooms, dressing rooms and storage in plan and elevation; draw ceiling heights, reveals and shading in section.
Report achieved geometry separately from unverified access targets; verify the source passage before turning a diagnostic into a required minimum.
stages.worked_example: Bedroom fixture contains six furniture objects. Review keeps the unknown chair as an obstacle. Moving a bedside table onto the bed must expose a physical clash even when it is marked as a bed accessory. Existing access thresholds remain unverified.
failures: Failure: replacing measured furniture by catalogue sizes. Remedy: retain extracted footprints and inspect disagreement.
Failure: plan fits but curtains collide with a wardrobe. Remedy: review opening and joinery elevations; return to Order if wall length changes.

stages.name: Systems
questions: Do you read in bed while someone else sleeps?
Which sounds or temperatures disturb you?
approval: Daylight glare blackout and scenes reviewed
Cooling ventilation acoustics power water coordinated
Equipment maintenance access shown
Measured light distinguished from comfort targets
Window sizes, shading and glass justified by the per-room thermal and daylight study
Consultant scope listed as missing: glare (DGP), HVAC, electrical, plumbing, structure
method: Make a room-by-room schedule for daylight, glare, blackout, sound, temperature, ventilation, sockets, water and controls; name unresolved targets.
Overlay luminaires, grilles, detectors, curtains, beams, ducts and access panels on the reflected ceiling plan and a service section.
Use existing direct-light arithmetic for diagnostic points. Total-light uniformity, glare, ventilation and thermal predictions require their appropriate methods and verified targets.
Run the per-room window study (window-to-wall ratio x orientation x shading x glass) for overheating hours, cooling load and daylight; recommend each room's window.
Prepare the consultant hand-off: room peak loads, reflected ceiling plan, sections, schedules and an IFC model. Glare, HVAC, electrical and plumbing stay missing until done.
stages.worked_example: Bedroom reader wants a separately controlled bedside task light and a dark sleeping scene. Existing photometric workflow can measure direct light; it cannot prove acoustic privacy or thermal comfort. A duct through the headboard bulkhead triggers a section and noise review.
failures: Failure: bright image treated as adequate lighting. Remedy: calculate the defined task plane and explain missing bounce/shadows.
Failure: ceiling conceals inaccessible equipment. Remedy: show removal path and access panel; reopen Rooms for lost height.

method: Schedule materials by room and exposure, with product evidence, sample status, cleaning and replacement access.
Draw representative floor-to-wall, window reveal, wet-area threshold, joinery-light and indoor-outdoor junctions; show layers and interfaces.
Coordinate drainage, weathering, acoustic seals and fixing zones with structure and services. Do not invent waterproofing assemblies without tested manufacturer details.
Pick every finish and FF&E item from the verified product library with a primary and an alternate from different ranges, oversampling the taste profile.
stages.worked_example: Bedroom study pairs timber joinery with a recessed task light: reserve accessible driver space and a removable panel. Garden threshold needs drainage and moisture detailing before the seamless appearance can be accepted.

method: Compare day/night views, measured model, plans, sections, interiors and landscape together. Show sightlines and routes that hero views can hide.
Bind render inputs and image files to the reviewed model and project revision using content hashes; rerun affected review after any change.
Trace every client requirement to an artifact; distinguish unresolved issues, rejected alternatives and accepted trade-offs. Presentation readiness does not authorize a real gate.
Estimate room acoustics from build-ups and finishes; mitigate with rugs, curtains, upholstery or panels, and record what remains open.
stages.worked_example: Pilot pavilion can look convincing in a garden view while its graph fails private access. Bedroom presentation must match its measured extract and rendering-input hashes; replacing an image or changing a model invalidates the binding.
failures: Failure: beautiful image suppresses unresolved glare. Remedy: include the issue in the presentation and keep approval readiness closed.
Failure: cached review survives a changed source edition. Remedy: invalidate evidence-dependent review and recheck applicability.
